George's dream answers by creating extraterrestrial enemies: an alien presence on the Moon and a threat to Earth give rival nations a common opponent, unifying humanity through war. Portland and the wider world are reshaped again, while Haber's institute and public stature grow with every reality he has induced. George sees that Haber's stated aims remain idealistic, but his faith in deliberate control prevents him from recognizing the repeated violence of the results.

Further dreaming changes the aliens from a terrifying enemy into neighbors with whom humanity can communicate. Their presence establishes a new political balance rather than the simple victory Haber intended. Heather exists again in the altered world, now with gray skin, and George finds that a version of their bond has become part of reality. He tries to preserve the people he loves without issuing the kind of sweeping commands that have caused so much harm. Haber, however, interprets each unstable success as proof that the method needs a more capable director. He advances the Augmentor and prepares to bypass George's reluctance, aiming to acquire effective dreaming for himself rather than accept any limit on his power to redesign the world.

Haber completes his attempt to induce effective dreaming in himself, believing disciplined intention will produce the rational world that George could not. The experiment instead breaks down the boundaries of reality. Conflicting people, places, and histories flow together as Haber's dream becomes a formless nightmare. George crosses the disintegrating city and reaches the Augmentor, switching it off before the collapse becomes complete. A world stabilizes, but it is a composite rather than a restoration of any single lost history. Aliens remain part of life, and Haber is alive but mentally shattered and confined to care. George is released from the power and its coercive treatment. He later works peacefully for an alien-run business and encounters Heather Lelache once more. She does not remember their marriage in another version of reality and is not identical to that Heather. George accepts the present instead of forcing it to match his memory, and the two tentatively begin a new connection.

characters.description: A St. Louis animator and licensed vampire executioner. Anita begins the case with two unwanted mystical marks from Jean-Claude, the city's new master vampire, but still insists that her work and decisions are her own. She refuses animation jobs that require a human death and assists police when a crime appears to involve the raised dead.
characters.name: Anita Blake

characters.description: A wealthy businessman who offers Anita an extraordinary fee to raise a long-dead ancestor. Gaynor uses a wheelchair, expects money to overcome objections, and is unwilling to accept Anita's refusal when she explains that the proposed animation would require a human sacrifice.
characters.name: Harold Gaynor

characters.description: Owner of Animators, Inc. and Anita's employer. Bert is impressed by Gaynor's money and less attentive than Anita to the ethical boundary built into the requested job.
characters.name: Bert Vaughn

characters.description: Anita's friend and former teacher in the practice of raising the dead. Manny accompanies her when she consults a powerful vaudun practitioner, and his past knowledge of that circle is deeper than Anita first realized.
characters.name: Manuel Rodriguez

characters.description: A feared St. Louis vaudun priestess whom Anita consults about the power needed to raise an exceptionally old corpse. Dominga is courteous but controlling, and the practices Anita witnesses in her home cross boundaries Anita will not accept.
characters.name: Dominga Salvador

characters.description: The police detective who leads the Regional Preternatural Investigation Team. Dolph asks Anita to assess a series of deaths whose evidence suggests something far more powerful than an ordinary zombie.
characters.name: Rudolph Storr

characters.description: A detective on Dolph's squad. Zerbrowski uses irreverence to ease tense scenes, but he is an observant investigator who treats Anita as part of the working team.
characters.name: Zerbrowski

characters.description: The new master vampire of St. Louis. Jean-Claude wants Anita to acknowledge the bond created by the two marks he placed on her, while she refuses both the title and the personal claim he attaches to it.
characters.name: Jean-Claude

characters.description: A vaudun practitioner recently arrived in St. Louis after his brother's death. Burke has enough power to attract suspicion when the police seek someone capable of creating the killer they are tracking.
characters.name: John Burke

characters.description: A former companion of Gaynor who understands his private affairs and the purpose behind his demand to raise an ancestor. She is frightened of him but willing to help Anita establish what he is doing.
characters.name: Wanda

characters.description: One of Gaynor's enforcers. Bruno relies on intimidation and physical force to make his employer's demands effective.
characters.name: Bruno

characters.description: An enforcer working with Bruno for Gaynor. Tommy helps confine and threaten people who stand between Gaynor and the secret he wants from his dead ancestor.
characters.name: Tommy

recaps.ending: The force behind the killings is traced to Dominga Salvador's forbidden vaudun work and Harold Gaynor's effort to obtain a family secret from a long-dead ancestor. Gaynor has treated human lives as material for the sacrifice required by that animation, and Wanda is killed after helping Anita. Gaynor's men hold Anita at a cemetery and force the ritual forward. The fresh sacrifice gives Anita far more power than an ordinary raising. Instead of producing only the ancestor Gaynor wants, she calls the cemetery's dead and turns that power against her captors. Gaynor and his enforcers are overwhelmed by the dead they sought to exploit. Dominga's role in creating and controlling the murderous zombie is exposed and her operation is ended. Anita solves the police case and prevents Gaynor from obtaining the information he wanted, but she does so by using a scale of power that confirms how dangerous her own animator abilities can become under the wrong conditions. Jean-Claude remains master of St. Louis and continues pressing his claim that Anita is his human servant; she continues to reject it.
recaps.in_short: Anita refuses millionaire Harold Gaynor's request to raise an ancestor because a corpse that old requires a human sacrifice. At the same time, Dolph's police team asks her to examine a series of deaths caused by an abnormally powerful zombie. Her inquiries lead through vaudun practitioner Dominga Salvador, Anita's former teacher Manny Rodriguez, newcomer John Burke, and Wanda, a woman with knowledge of Gaynor's plans. Anita learns that Gaynor wants a secret from his ancestor and is prepared to supply the necessary victim, while Dominga's forbidden work lies behind the killer zombie. Gaynor's men seize Anita and use Wanda's death to power the final raising. Anita draws on that power to call the cemetery's dead and turns them against Gaynor and his enforcers. The murder case and Gaynor's scheme end, while Anita remains marked by Jean-Claude and troubled by the destructive reach of her own abilities.

recaps.text: Previously: Anita Blake raises the dead professionally and serves as a court-authorized vampire executioner in St. Louis. While investigating vampire murders, she was coerced by Nikolaos, the city's master vampire, and worked uneasily with vampire hunter Edward and the vampire Jean-Claude. The killer was an animator sustaining his own continued existence through the deaths, under Nikolaos's protection. Anita and Edward destroyed the operation, and Anita killed Nikolaos. Jean-Claude survived and became St. Louis's new master. During the case he placed two mystical marks on Anita. He treats the bond as the beginning of a human-servant relationship; Anita rejects that interpretation and remains determined to control her own life.

Harold Gaynor offers Animators, Inc. a very large fee to raise one of his ancestors. Anita explains that a corpse dead for that long cannot be called back by ordinary methods: the ritual would require a human sacrifice. She refuses, despite her employer Bert's interest in the money. Gaynor does not regard her refusal as final. The request establishes both his object - information held by the dead relative - and his willingness to seek an animator who will cross a boundary Anita considers absolute.

Dolph brings Anita into a police investigation after deaths at a family home show signs of a supernatural attacker. Anita concludes that the killer is a zombie of exceptional strength, which implies that someone used a human death to raise it. Seeking expertise, she visits Dominga Salvador with her former teacher Manny Rodriguez. Dominga's command of vaudun is formidable, but Anita finds evidence that she binds human spirits into obedient dead bodies and refuses her proposed cooperation. Manny admits that his own past with Dominga included practices he abandoned. The police case and Gaynor's demand now share the same central question: who is willing and able to spend a human life for a powerful raising?

The killer strikes again, and the police struggle to contain something that does not behave like a decaying, mindless corpse. John Burke, a strong vaudun practitioner newly arrived after his brother's death, becomes a possible suspect because he has the necessary knowledge, but Anita finds no reason to treat power alone as proof. Jean-Claude continues pressing her to accept the two marks linking them and the status he says follows from them. Anita keeps the vampire dispute separate from her work while comparing the murder scenes, Gaynor's request, and Dominga's hidden practices.

Wanda, a former companion of Gaynor, helps Anita understand why he is determined to raise his ancestor: he expects the dead man to disclose a valuable family secret. Gaynor's enforcers, Bruno and Tommy, apply increasing pressure and make clear that he is prepared to provide the sacrifice Anita refused to make. Evidence also narrows the police inquiry toward a commissioned raising rather than an uncontrolled natural event. Anita's attempt to protect witnesses and stop the next killing puts her directly against Gaynor's organization.

Anita connects the murderous zombie to forbidden vaudun work and to the same circle serving Gaynor's plans. Dominga's respectable public position conceals an operation that can create and command dead bodies through human sacrifice. Gaynor's interest is narrower but equally dangerous: he wants the ancestor raised regardless of who must die. Wanda's cooperation places her in immediate danger, and Anita's efforts to stop the ritual end with Gaynor's men taking control of the location and the people needed to perform it.

Dominga Salvador is exposed as the practitioner whose forbidden methods produced the powerful killer zombie, while Harold Gaynor is the client willing to fund and exploit human sacrifice for his own family secret. After Wanda helps Anita, Gaynor has her killed and uses the death to force the cemetery ritual. The sacrifice gives Anita enough power to raise far more than the single ancestor Gaynor requested. She calls the cemetery's dead and directs them against Gaynor and his enforcers, ending his scheme and the immediate threat. Dominga's operation is broken and the police killings are explained. Anita survives with a clearer understanding that her animator power can become immense when fueled by a human death. Jean-Claude remains the city's master and continues to call her his human servant because of his two marks, a claim Anita still refuses.
